overview: Force Pull is a novice-level light side technique classified under Telekinesis. Draws objects, weapons, or opponents toward the wielder through concentrated telekinetic attraction. Luke Skywalker's retrieval of his lightsaber from beneath Cloud City remains one of the most iconic demonstrations of this technique.
history:
Force scholars trace Force Pull across eras recorded in holocrons, Jedi Archives data-tapes, and Sith tombs on Korriban and Dromund Kaas. Practitioners documented in Films · Empire Strikes Back · Return of the Jedi · The Last Jedi established the modern understanding of how this ability manifests in combat, meditation, and ritual.

During the Old Republic and Sith Empire conflicts, masters drilled Force Pull into initiates as part of the standard curriculum for telekinesis specialisation. Surviving battle logs from the Clone Wars and Galactic Civil War show the technique adapted to blaster-era warfare, starfighter engagements, and close-quarters lightsaber duels.

In the sequel era, surviving texts and oral traditions kept knowledge of Force Pull alive even as the Jedi Temple fell and the Sith assumed new forms. Each generation reinterpreted the power through its own doctrine while the underlying Force mechanism — channelled midi-chlorian symbiosis and focused will — remained constant.

The Jedi teach that this ability must serve life, consent, and the greater good — never domination or fear.
significance:
Force Pull exemplifies how telekinesis abilities shape Force doctrine on the light side. At novice mastery, users balance raw potential against discipline, emotional control, and the moral weight of their choices.

Historians note that armies and orders rose or fell partly on how widely and wisely this technique was taught. A single master of Force Pull could turn a skirmish, break a siege, or unravel an enemy's will before blades crossed.

For students today — in academies, hidden enclaves, or alone with ancient texts — Force Pull remains a benchmark of telekinesis proficiency across the Star Wars saga.
